issues.issue: The 50% TSS reduction figures (68 (45.9%) Jakafi vs 8 (5.3%) placebo) are presented as counts/percentages but the citation quote only gives '68 (45.9) 8 (5.3)' without labeling them as patient counts and placebo; percentages labeled as placebo '5.3%' are supported, but the claim 'P < 0.0001' is applied to the TSS endpoint without a citation that ties that p-value to the symptom score result.

Text states 'Jakafi N=155, Placebo N=154' which is supported by the citation, but the same cited quote also contains Study 2 arms (N=146 / N=73), a stitched multi-study header row that could be mis-attributed.
The number '48' (Week 48) in the result text is not contained in any citation quote for this field (uncited_numbers flag); the Week 48 timepoint is only cited in the endpoint field, not the result.

The P < 0.0001 cited for Study 2 comes from the same 'P-value < 0.0001 < 0.0001' quote at line 225, which belongs to Study 1's spleen table (65/1 and 41/28.5 are in different columns); the p-value for Study 2's Week 48 endpoint is not clearly supported by a Study-2-specific citation.
uncited_numbers flags '1' in 'Study 1'; this is a false positive — it is a study label, not an efficacy/safety number.

uncited_numbers flags '3' in '3 year follow-up' context; the '3-year' is not in the summary citations but is a non-efficacy PMC detail — low-severity false positive, though the summary itself does not cite the PREA/3-year number source directly.

The summary claims the drug was 'first-in-class' and that the sponsor was 'exempt from PREA pediatric assessment requirements due to orphan designation' — the PREA exemption is supported, but 'first-in-class' is sourced correctly; however the phrase 'two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials' conflates the pivotal (Study 1) and supporting (Study 2) trials, which the review distinguishes as pivotal vs supporting.

The detail text and one citation misquote 'post-essential thrombocytopenia myelofibrosis' from the review whereas the indication field uses 'post-essential thrombocythemia myelofibrosis'; the source quote actually contains the erroneous 'thrombocytopenia', so the mismatch originates in the document, not the card.

The receipt date is June 3, 2011 with a PDUFA goal date of December 4, 2011 (~6 months), which is consistent with a Priority Review for an orphan oncology NME; priority_review.present=false may be an incorrect omission of a designation the drug plainly had.
